5. Mr.M.A.Wahab Mia, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant has firstly taken us through the First information Report, the charge, the depositions of the witnesses, the statement of the accused Abu Baker Siddique under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and other materials and record including the impugned Judgment and then he assailed the appellant's conviction and sentence on various grounds. His first ground of attack is that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence against the appellant is wholly bad in law and on facts and the prosecution has hopelessly failed to establish the ingredients of the offences under Section 364 as well as under Section 325 of the Penal Code by cogent reliable and sufficient evidence. The 2nd ground of attacking the judgment is that there has been enough of embellishment of the prosecution case as made out in the F.I.R. lodged on 30.7.86 and that admittedly there was an earlier information given to the Police by the informant about the occurrence and the Police already started acting upon the same hence the alleged F.I.R. could not be treated as the F.I.R. under Section 154 Cr. P.C. according to law. The 3rd point of attack is that the prosecution has failed to produce in court the most vital witnesses, particularly the victim Samaun and the Investigating Officer of the Case who were charge-sheeted witnesses and for their non-production, the learned Additional Sessions Judge ought to have drawn adverse presumption against the prosecution case and particularly for non-production of the 1.0., the accused appellant has been deprived of cross-examining him to bring out the contradictions in the evidence of the P.Ws. and as a result the defence has been seriously prejudiced. Lastly the learned Advocate for the appellant contends that the evidence of the P.Ws. suffers from material contradictions and inconsistencies, but the learned Additional Sessions Judge without noticing the same wrongly relied upon such evidences of the witnesses and illegally passed the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence against the appellant which are liable to be set aside. 

 13. In our view for non-production of the victim Liton @ Samaun, the doctor who allegedly gave medical treatment to the said victim, the I. O  the local Chairman and some other independent witnesses an adverse presumption against the prosecution case ought to have been drawn by the trial court.
